iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment: Partial-to-moderate. The westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletin series is confirmed as the primary authoritative source for California WNV surveillance data, and at least two 2024-season bulletins (download_ids 5061 and 5147) have been surfaced with snippets showing human case counts by county. The CDC Historic Data page (1999–2025) is confirmed as the federal cross-validation source. The LA County DPH domain appeared in iteration 2 results. However, no result has a confirmed publication date explicitly within 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31; bulletin week-ending dates must be verified by a downstream fetching agent. Deaths and hospitalization counts for August 2024 specifically have not been confirmed in any snippet. The CDC 2024 state-level data table was not directly retrieved with California-specific numeric content. County-level locality detail beyond LA, Butte, and Kern is absent from confirmed snippets.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: High for primary sources. westnile.ca.gov is the official CDPH WNV surveillance portal (ca.gov domain, CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section authorship). CDC historic data page is a federal .gov source using ArboNET surveillance data. publichealth.lacounty.gov is the official LA County Department of Public Health domain. These three source types meet the highest trust threshold for public health surveillance data. News sources (latimes.com, abcnews.com) are credible regional/national outlets but are secondary to official agency sources. Out-of-scope, social media, and non-authoritative sources (illinois DPH, facebook, instagram, cola.org, vdci.net) should be excluded or treated as low-trust.
